roads.name: Marmot Road
words: Sweeping and steady: 17 curves in 5.7 miles.
From 4,033 to 5,647 ft, with 1,731 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every sweeper in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 80 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 0.30 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this takes Alberta's 80 km/h.

roads.name: Pyramid Lake Road
words: Properly twisty: 32 curves in 4.3 miles, about 7 a mile.
From 3,478 to 3,923 ft, with 589 ft of up and down along the way.
45 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
